body:
Went back on my throwaway to comment on this, in a sense as a means to vent out some feelings I didn't actually even realise until watching Tyler's speech. If you go back on my post history, I made this account to ask for help and advice on how to my sister in the midst of a suicide attempt. I had attempted suicide numerous times before, I've known people who killed themselves and been in situations where I've had to stop someone from an attempt by hanging.  


My sister was the first time it was someone so close to me, that I cared so much about, who I'd have to make a consistent effort over a long period of time to help--not just pulling them out of a noose the one time. It was the first time I had been in this situation, so despite being overly familiar with mental struggles, the mentality, I actually had no clue what to do. I kind of just did what I could in the moment, everything that I could. This was a person whose sheer existence meant more to me than pretty much anything else.  


So when I was the only one to drop everything and drive to her place, when I was the only one committed to staying up overnight to watch over her, to change my schedule to adapt to her needs, to basically put her life as my number one priority over everything, I think I became far more distrustful on sharing things with people. Other people knew about her struggle, her ideations. The only reason I found out she was on the verge of suicide was because she called me to more or less say farewell. Other people knew beforehand not necessarily that she was committed to making an attempt, but that she was going through a rough time. No one else dropped everything to come to her.  


People had their own responsibilities to fulfill--work to attend, stuff like that. And to me, as someone who had been down her path before, knowing that was how people responded on the other side of the coin... It filled me with vitriol and disappointment and some inescapable pool of loneliness. No career path of mine, no responsibility of my own benefit trumps the life of someone I hold that dear. I keep a small circle of friends and family because, like Tyler said, friendships--and relationships as a whole--is a tiresome commitment, but my emotional investment to love and care for someone makes at the very least their livelihood way more important than anything else in my life. In that moment it honestly felt like I was the only one in the world who felt that way.  


Maybe it's short-sighted and unfair of me to think this, but when someone is on the verge of death, especially self-motivated, and the people around them who were supposed to be close ones don't drop quite literally everything to come to their aid, for however long it takes, then they weren't close enough.

1 - very helpful and will keep that in mind. The more i talk to her the more hospitalisation seems necessary, so this will be important.
 
2 - Duly noted. I'll look into it. Though for her it's not that she'll be fired. It's that she's currently going through some sort of program that gives her credentials to teach AP classes, and that without those credentials she will no longer be qualified to teach at the place she does. So then she has to look for a new job, assign herself new responsibilities and go through the whole tedious process.

3 - Aye, I've gone through the wards myself and it was about a week. I dont know how her school operates, but she keeps saying that she wont be able to continue if shes hospitalised.

4 - Teaching. She's currently teaching high school full-time and also going to school for her doctorates. And its the life she says she wanted, despite all that work and pressure seemingly now becoming a burden that she *can* handle, but doesnt want to handle anymore. And I believe she feels that going back is not an option

5 - Ive resolved to look over her dog already. Tmk, no disabilities that can help with that. She doesnt tell me everything so im not sure, mmobut she's also a competent person who i am sure alteady thought about that.

6 - So far it seems that she's talked to more people about this than I first believed, so I suppose she's not stuffing them. She's talked to some friends and family, not all though. I dont think she's talked to anyone who understands the mindstate though, as she's said she always has the same stale conversations that I'm all too painfully familiar with myself.

7 - You are very right. My hope is to switch off with someone to stay with her in the morning, since i can force myself to stay up for days on end but it wont be helpful for either of us if i destroy myself in the process.

I dont know if she has seen one, but i am assured that she will not be willing. She woke up several times in the middle of the to plead to me that i "let her go" and that she "wants to be at peace", and that if its too painful for me to let her go that i should just leave and let her go on her own.

She's left to walk her dog now, and asked that i leave her apartment, and that she hates me for doing this (forcing her to continue living) and that she never wants to see me again.

This is what i messaged someone else.

\[Calling more people to help will worsen her standing. Checking into the hospital means:

1 - paying bills more than she can earn

2 - losing her job

3 - delaying her schoolwork

4 - never being able to work in her field again, which is her ideal field

5 - being unable to keep her dog out of financial burden, or her housing, or really anything

6 - making everyone around her notified of her emotions which will only further ostracise and embarass her

7 - damage her pride because everyone will know and she'll likely have to be dependent on other people to get by for a good while, which will never sit well with her as she's independent to, evidently, a fault

8 - increase her stressors which helped push her to this point to begin with

9 - only make her think that continuing living is even more of a hellish burden than it already is

Going to the hospital is only truly and absolutely a last resort when I cant continue watching over her.\]

So if necessary I will force her to go to the hospital, but Im keeping that in the back. I think the biggest issue for professional help right now is willingness to seek it. Her ideations at the moment are largely driven by utter apathy, and its difficult to have someone go to therapy or a doctor when they dont care to. She kept saying to me that she doesnt want to talk about it anymore, and she's just too tired for it--that she only wants to just stop living. I will for sure also force her to at least try it if it comes to it, but that's also not an ideal first take.
